from torch import Tensor

from .adam import Adam, adam
from .optimizer import (
    _capturable_doc,
    _differentiable_doc,
    _foreach_doc,
    _fused_doc,
    _maximize_doc,
    _params_doc,
    ParamsT,
    StateDict,
)


__all__ = ["AdamW", "adamw"]


class AdamW(Adam):
    def __init__(
        self,
        params: ParamsT,
        lr: float | Tensor = 1e-3,
        betas: tuple[float | Tensor, float | Tensor] = (0.9, 0.999),
        eps: float = 1e-8,
        weight_decay: float = 1e-2,
        amsgrad: bool = False,
        *,
        maximize: bool = False,
        foreach: bool | None = None,
        capturable: bool = False,
        differentiable: bool = False,
        fused: bool | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(
            params,
            lr,
            betas,
            eps,
            weight_decay,
            amsgrad,
            foreach=foreach,
            maximize=maximize,
            capturable=capturable,
            differentiable=differentiable,
            fused=fused,
            decoupled_weight_decay=True,
        )

    # Preserve decoupled_weight_decay from AdamW for backwards compatibility. The following
    # guarantees that decoupled_weight_decay will always be True for loading any state into
    # AdamW
    def __setstate__(self, state: StateDict) -> None:
        super().__setstate__(state)
        for group in self.param_groups:
            group["decoupled_weight_decay"] = True

optimizer_semantics_probe.note: Measured on a throwaway parameter: the variant listed in 'measured_variant' is the one that reproduces this PyTorch build's update bit for bit.

notes: Round-trip check: the decoded sign/exponent/fraction re-encode to the observed raw word.
numpy and torch reinterpretation paths are compared against each other, so a systematic error in one would show up as a disagreement.
Real training: torch loss.backward() and optimizer.step() only. No gradient is assigned, no parameter value is written outside the optimizer, and no trajectory is precomputed.
The float64 track is a separate real run of the same forward shape in a different precision. It is a reference, not ground truth.
